name: application-menu-item-row
title: Menu Item Row
description: A restaurant menu row with dish name, description, dietary tags, price, and an add-to-order button, at both a detailed single-item scale and a compact multi-item list.
useWhen: Displaying a restaurant or food-ordering menu where each item needs a description, dietary tags, and a clear add action.
Browsing available dishes before they're added to an order — the browsing state, not the already-added cart state.
avoidWhen: The item has already been added to an order and needs quantity/remove controls — use cart-line-item for that stage instead.
You need a photo-forward card layout rather than a text row — a dish card with an image is a better fit.
responsiveBehavior: The detailed row uses a flexible text column with a fixed-size add button pinned to the right; the compact list keeps the same right-aligned price/button pairing per row so multiple items stay visually aligned.
accessibility: The icon-only add button carries an aria-label naming the specific dish, not a generic 'Add', so multiple items remain distinguishable to screen reader users.
Dietary tags (VEGAN, GF) are rendered as visible text badges, not icon-only, so their meaning doesn't depend on recognizing an icon.
Price is always plain text adjacent to the item, independent of any visual styling.

variants.title: Detailed row
variants.description: Single dish with name, dietary tag badges, full description, price, and a circular add button
accessibility: The add button's aria-label names the specific dish.
